sentences.text: Pseudhesperosuchus belongs to the sphenosuchians, a group of early crocodylomorphs.
Recent analysis revealed the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was immature, indicated by open neurocentral sutures on its neck vertebrae.
José Bonaparte named this genus in 1969.
The skull is nearly complete but poorly preserved, containing some misidentified bones and artificial holes from preparation.
This animal lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
A 2002 study found Pseudhesperosuchus to have an unresolved phylogenetic position, neither closer to true crocodiles nor to Sphenosuchus.
